newsitem.title: USA: Merck & Co buyback a plus - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Merck & Co buyback a plus - analysts.

text.p: Merck & Co's announcement on Tuesday that it would buy back another $5 billion in shares is a positive, analysts said.
"This only makes a strong story stronger," said David Maris, an analyst with Aros Securities.

"It's an indication how strong their intermediate- and longer-term outlook is. They have the largest cash flow in the industry and this is a way to return some of that to the shareholders without limiting their options" on acquisitions.
Merck said it would buy back $5 billion of its common shares, in addition to a $3 billion buyback already underway. Merck's shares closed off 5/8 at 97-3/4 on moderate volume.
Standard & Poor's affirmed its triple "A" corporate credit and senior unsecured debt ratings following the announcement of the $5 bilion share repurchase agreement.

"Given the strong cash generation afforded by the company's successful pharmaceutical products, the funding of this program will not affect overall credit quality, " the Standard & Poor's analysts said.
Richard Vietor, an analyst at Merrill Lynch, called the move "positive but not dramatic."
He said although the $5 billion figure was "huge ... in the context of Merck, 50 million shares out of 1.2 billion (is) only four percent of outstanding shares."
Maris said he had set a $115 12-month price target on the shares this month and reiterated a buy recommendation.
Earlier on Tuesday Merck also reported that it had raised its dividend to $0.42 a share from $0.40 a share.
